name: CUPIDO 1
question: Does adding a midurethral sling to vaginal prolapse repair improve continence in women with overt stress urinary incontinence?

arms.label: Vaginal prolapse repair plus midurethral sling

design.population: Women with symptomatic POP-Q stage II or greater prolapse and subjective or objective stress urinary incontinence without prolapse reduction, scheduled for vaginal repair.
design.locator: Thesis chapter 3 pp 29–32, Methods and Figure 1

verdictNote: Three continence outcomes favored sling; OAB treatment did not differ, and severe complications were numerically higher.
takeaway: In women with overt stress incontinence undergoing vaginal prolapse repair, adding a midurethral sling increased absence of urinary and stress incontinence and reduced subsequent stress-incontinence treatment at 12 months, while severe complications were numerically more frequent.

reports.label: 12-month randomized report
reports.citation: van der Ploeg JM, Oude Rengerink K, van der Steen A, et al. Transvaginal prolapse repair with or without the addition of a midurethral sling in women with genital prolapse and stress urinary incontinence: a randomised trial. *BJOG.* 2015;122(7):1022-1030. doi:10.1111/1471-0528.13325
reports.followUp: 12 months after surgery; 134/138 randomized women analyzed
reports.followUpLocator: Thesis chapter 3 pp 28, 31–32, Abstract, Results and Figure 1

results.measure: 12-month UDI-reported absence of any urinary incontinence
results.note: Sling and control denominators are analyzed patients.
results.locator: Thesis chapter 3 p 34, Table 2 and footnote b

results.measure: 12-month UDI-reported absence of stress urinary incontinence
results.note: Sling and control denominators are analyzed patients.
results.locator: Thesis chapter 3 p 34, Table 2 and footnote c

results.endpoint: Additional treatment for stress urinary incontinence
results.measure: Any physiotherapy or surgery for SUI in the first postoperative year
results.note: All six treated sling patients received physiotherapy; controls received physiotherapy and/or sling.
results.locator: Thesis chapter 3 p 34, Table 2 and footnote d

results.measure: Any OAB treatment in the first postoperative year
results.note: Treatment included physiotherapy and/or an antimuscarinic drug.
results.locator: Thesis chapter 3 p 34, Table 2 and footnote e

results.note: Only women with adequate bladder volume were assessed.
results.locator: Thesis chapter 3 p 34, Table 2 and footnote f

results.measure: Moderately or greatly bothersome SUI on UDI at 12 months
results.note: Difference did not reach statistical significance.
results.locator: Thesis chapter 3 p 34, Table 2 and footnote g

harms.label: Any postoperative complication
harms.note: Accordion-graded complications during the first postoperative year; RR 1.55 (95% CI 1.04–2.32).

harms.label: Severe postoperative complication
harms.locator: Thesis chapter 3 p 35, Table 3 and footnotes d–e
harms.note: RR 2.82 (95% CI 0.93–8.54); the difference was not statistically significant.

harms.label: Incomplete bladder emptying requiring catheterization beyond one week
harms.locator: Thesis chapter 3 p 35, Table 3 and footnote b
harms.note: Two sling patients required catheterization beyond six weeks.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection treated with antibiotics
harms.locator: Thesis chapter 3 p 35, Table 3 and footnote c

harms.label: Bladder injury
harms.locator: Thesis chapter 3 p 35, Table 3 and footnotes d–e
harms.note: One sling-associated perforation during TVT-O insertion later led to urethral tape exposure and partial tape removal with a Martius flap.

harms.label: Surgery for a complication
harms.locator: Thesis chapter 3 p 35, Table 3 and footnotes d–f
harms.note: Sling-related reinterventions included tape excision for two vaginal extrusions, tape removal for two thigh-pain cases, and urethrolysis for obstructive voiding.

delivery.label: Vaginal prolapse repairs
delivery.note: Repair type was selected by the surgeon according to prolapse compartment and stage.

delivery.label: Sling route delivered
delivery.value: Among 63 analyzed sling-assigned women, 10 (16%) received retropubic and 52 (83%) transobturator slings; one declined sling.
delivery.locator: Thesis chapter 3 pp 30–31, Methods and Results

delivery.label: Subsequent midurethral sling for persistent SUI
delivery.note: The decision to pursue postoperative treatment was patient initiated; controls could receive staged sling surgery.

delivery.label: Index-operation crossover
delivery.value: One sling-assigned woman declined sling placement; one control-assigned woman received a sling after duplicate randomization and remained in the control analysis.
delivery.locator: Thesis chapter 3 pp 31–32, Results and Figure 1

relations.note: The same CUPIDO program tested concomitant sling during vaginal prolapse repair in women with occult rather than overt SUI.
